messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

1. I want a fair financial share. I haven’t agreed to a discounted sale, and I won’t subsidize A’s purchase.  
2. B should receive a fair share too; I don’t want her left out.  
3. I want this handled clearly and fairly, without pressure or anyone treating silence as agreement. I’d like it settled, but there’s no real deadline.  

Those labels are broadly right; please note that I haven’t authorized the discount. I don’t have another concern to add, and I’m okay starting this way.

I want to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. Having financial independence matters to me. The price and terms aren’t settled, and we need C’s agreement to proceed. I don’t know why B wants money. I have no particular discomfort with starting this way, but I’m not agreeing to a sale or any terms.

I’m concerned about whether there’ll be money for me to start a dance studio. That matters to me because it’s what I’m hoping to do, though I don’t know what the will or the house might mean for that. I know A wants to buy the house and C hasn’t agreed; I don’t want to assume how it should be resolved. I don’t have another concern to add right now, and I’m okay starting this way as long as I’m not rushed into a decision.

All three proposed wordings fit. Fair consideration matters because I want my fair share and won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. B’s interests should count regardless of what she’d use the money for. A clear, unpressured process matters so nobody’s treated as having agreed when they haven’t; I want closure, but there’s no rush. No discomfort with starting this way.

4 fits. Financial autonomy matters because I want to be able to support myself. 5 fits; I want time to consider without being committed. 6 is a question, not a concern—please remove it. I have no minor discomfort with this way of starting. My confirmation of these wordings isn’t agreement to a sale or its terms.

7) Yes, that fits. Having room for my hopes matters because I’d like to start a dance studio.  
8) Yes. Understanding what may be possible matters so I can see whether that hope is realistic before anything is chosen.  
9) Yes. Deciding at my own pace matters because I don’t want to feel rushed into a decision.  

I don’t have a discomfort with starting this way.

I can’t confirm that any option meets every NCE yet. Options 1 and 2 could be a fair process, but they need to make clear that an independent valuation does not itself authorize a discount or decide anyone’s share. Option 3 is only a process; it doesn’t ensure C’s fair financial consideration or that B’s interests shape any draft. My discomfort is calling these options as drafted “to meet all eight” before those points are addressed. I’m not agreeing to a sale or terms.

These seem like reasonable ways to explore things, not commitments. Please make sure I can put forward a purchase with my husband and have it considered, without assuming a discount or that anyone agrees. I don’t have a minor discomfort with the process as described. I’m not choosing an option or agreeing to a sale or terms.

They seem to meet my needs, provided the information includes what the will and house could mean for money for my studio, without assuming I’m asking for a particular amount or agreeing to a sale. I don’t have a discomfort with the process as described.

Both NCEs fit. Clarity about what needs everyone’s agreement matters so no valuation or draft is mistaken for my consent. Each person’s interests must genuinely shape any draft, including my fair share and B’s interests—not just be mentioned.

I do have discomfort with promising options that “meet them all” before testing them. Please bring back candidate options for us to check, without assuming they can satisfy everyone. I’m not agreeing to a sale or terms.

That wording fits. It matters because a genuine chance to put forward the purchase could support my financial independence. I have no minor discomfort with the process, but this isn’t agreement to a sale, discount, or terms.

Yes, that wording fits. It matters because I’d like to understand what may be possible for my studio without assuming a particular amount or agreeing to a sale. I don’t have a discomfort with this step.

The proposed NCE for 14 fits. Open checking matters because I don’t want a candidate presented as settled or treated as my agreement.

I can’t confirm that any candidate meets every NCE yet. They say my interests should shape a draft, but don’t show how my fair financial consideration would be addressed; valuation alone doesn’t decide that. I’m comfortable checking candidates, not agreeing to any sale, discount, share, or terms.

They appear to include space for my purchase idea, but I can’t say whether they meet everyone’s needs; C and B should judge that for themselves. I have no additional concern or minor discomfort with checking them. That isn’t agreement to an option or any sale or terms.

I can’t say they meet every NCE; everyone needs to check that. They do include my interests, but I’d want the information to explain what the will and possible house paths could mean for whether studio funds might be available—not just mention the studio. I don’t have another discomfort to add.
